abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are mediated by highly specific molecular recognition, and their interfaces provide a basis for designing highly selective peptide biorecognition elements for biosensing. Here we introduce a structure-based biomimetic strategy that allows recognizing a single target protein through both its homo- and hetero-interaction interfaces. We targeted the needle protein PrgI of the Salmonella typhimurium (ST) Type III Secretion System with two peptides: one derived from the PrgI oligomerization interface (residues 31-46, homo-interaction) and one from the PrgI-binding interface of the tip protein SipD (residues 291-305, hetero-interaction). Flow cytometry confirmed that both peptides selectively bind to ST. Following immobilization on gold electrodes, the peptides formed label-free electrochemical sensors that enabled impedimetric (EIS) detection of ST within 10 minutes, with a limit of detection of approximately 5 CFU/mL and linear ranges of 102-108; CFU/mL in PBS and 102-108; CFU/mL in an orange juice food-matrix model. These results establish native PPI interfaces, targeted through both homo- and hetero-interactions, as a general design principle for selective peptide ligands in electrochemical pathogen biosensing.
